clue.text: City somewhere between Uzbekistan and Bulgaria

indicators.note: and simply sets the second country's letters after the first's, in the order the clue names them
somewhere says only part of the first country's name is used, its opening stretch dropped
between, said of the second country, says only part of its name is used, its tail dropped

explanation.surface: A geography question placing a city on the map between two countries.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are the tail of Uzbekistan (losing UZBEK) and the head of Bulgaria (losing GARIA); 'and' just joins them. The surface is also true: the city lies between those countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Istanbul is the largest city in Turkey, straddling Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Merciful Pope left out material used for bonding

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is removed from the pope's name

parts.note: clement means merciful, and Clement is the name of several popes

explanation.surface: A kindly pontiff being excluded from something, followed by a builder's material.
explanation.definitionFit: Cement is the binding powder that sets to hold bricks, stone and aggregate together.

clue.text: Initial sighting of submarine missile — quite aggressive!

indicators.note: initial asks for only the opening letter of the word sighting

parts.note: Trident is the ballistic missile launched from British and American submarines

explanation.surface: A naval warning on first spotting a sub-launched missile, with an exclamation at its hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice or manner is harsh and forceful, assertive to the point of aggression.

clue.text: Weather permitting, wearing garment created from recycled material made in Jersey?

indicators.note: wearing places the abbreviation inside the garment, as if dressed in it

parts.note: a coat is an outer garment
WP is the standard abbreviation for weather permitting

explanation.surface: Fashion copy about an eco-friendly garment of recycled fabric made on the island of Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey is a Channel Island and also a breed of dairy cow; the recycled material is dung, used as fertiliser or fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowpat is a dropping produced by a cow, and a Jersey cow is one breed.

clue.text: Mother cradling head of science teacher

indicators.note: cradling means holding the next letter inside

parts.note: mater is Latin, and old public-school slang, for mother

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of science

explanation.surface: A mother holding the head of the school's science teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Master is an old-fashioned title for a schoolteacher, especially a male one in Britain.

clue.text: Tummy upset? Stupid, led astray!

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word for stupid upside down, reading it upwards

parts.note: dim means stupid

indicators.note: led astray means the letters of led wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone with stomach trouble, dismissed as a fool who has been led astray.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle is an informal word for the waist or belly area of the body.

clue.text: Hit a bloke sticking his oar in

definitions.meaning: a blow, as in a ... of the bat

definitions.text: a bloke sticking his oar in
definitions.meaning: in rowing, the oarsman nearest the stern who sets the pace for the crew

explanation.surface: Someone striking a man who keeps interfering in others' business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticking his oar in' means meddling in the surface, but here it is literal: the rower who sets the rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroke is a blow, and also the name of the rower who sets the crew's rate.

clue.text: English fiancée regularly crashed motor

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth of fiancée

explanation.surface: An English bride-to-be whose car has crashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' looks like an anagram signal but nothing is rearranged; it only colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine is the motor that powers a vehicle or machine.

clue.text: Plastic syringe can't have sharpness

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so these letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that a plastic syringe cannot be sharp enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringency is sharpness or severity of tone or taste, a biting quality.

clue.text: Commercial program sampling a review of Google raw data

indicators.note: review of says the hidden letters are read backwards
sampling takes a small run of letters from within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Software that sifts through a search giant's raw data.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'sampling' in the definition, but it is the signal for the hidden letters; the definition is 'Commercial program' alone. 'review of' reads the hidden run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Adware is software that displays advertisements, a program existing for commercial ends.

clue.text: Miss knocking back lager with lad at wedding

indicators.note: knocking back means the lager's name is read in reverse, with a hint of drinking

parts.note: pils is a pale Pilsner-style lager
a page is a boy attendant at a wedding

explanation.surface: A young woman drinking lager with a lad at a wedding reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' is a noun here, a shortfall, not a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Slippage is a falling short of a target, a miss in schedule or value.

clue.text: Facile government politician

parts.note: a Lib is a Liberal politician

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a smooth-talking member of the government.
explanation.definitionFit: Glib and facile both describe speech that is fluent but shallow.

clue.text: Held in Italian city, earl gets thinner

indicators.note: in puts the word for held inside the city

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy
pent, as in pent up, means held in

explanation.surface: An earl detained in an Italian city and losing weight there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thinner' reads as a comparative adjective but is a noun: a solvent for paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpentine is a solvent used to dilute oil paints, a paint thinner.

clue.text: When the pub shuts, Scot gets hammered with gin and lime

indicators.note: hammered means beaten out of shape, and drunk, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A Scotsman getting drunk on gin and lime at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Closing time is the hour at which a bar must stop serving and shut.

clue.text: Southern Yankee admits nothing concerning aid for 17 to avoid 10

definitions.note: uses the answers to 17 and 10, one steering and a miss or skid

indicators.note: admits means letting the word for nothing in between the two letters

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
nowt is northern English dialect for nothing
re means concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A Southerner from the US letting nothing in, followed by a cross-referenced puzzle phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at two other answers: 17 is the motorist, 10 a skid.
explanation.definitionFit: Winter tyres with deep tread help a motorist keep grip and not skid on icy roads.

clue.text: It helps tune in my Ice Age broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Tuning the radio to catch a programme about the Ice Age.
explanation.definitionFit: A magic eye was a glowing valve on old radios that showed when a station was correctly tuned.

clue.text: Digital whisky measure?

definitions.meaning: a digit of the hand, read as a noun
a depth of spirit gauged by a digit's width against the glass

explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' reads as an adjective about the measure, but it is its own definition: a digit of the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit of the hand, and also a tot of spirits as deep as one digit is wide.

clue.text: One steering French bank takes on debtor

indicators.note: takes on means the bank's word goes inside the debtor's letters

parts.note: DR is the accounting abbreviation for debtor
rive is French for a river bank

explanation.surface: A French bank taking on a debtor as a client.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests money, not a riverside, and 'Rive Gauche' is the Left Bank of Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver is the person who steers a vehicle.

clue.text: Stoned, Buffalo Bill's touring Maine for the witty banter

parts.note: high means intoxicated on drugs

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the showman's surname surrounds the state abbreviation

parts.note: Buffalo Bill was the showman William Cody
ME is the postal abbreviation for Maine

explanation.surface: A drug-addled Wild West showman touring New England, playing it for laughs.
explanation.definitionFit: High comedy is sophisticated comedy of wit and clever dialogue rather than slapstick.

clue.text: Hour-old over-the-counter hot grog

parts.note: OTC is the abbreviation for over-the-counter, used of medicines
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A stale hot toddy bought from a counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hootch is slang for alcoholic liquor, especially cheap or illicit spirit, as is grog.

clue.text: Annual Yuletide vacation on Australian Railway

indicators.note: vacation means emptying the word, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A yearly Christmas holiday taken on an Australian train.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearly and annual both mean happening once every year.

clue.text: It's bloody Al …

definitions.meaning: blood that has been shed, which is literally bloody

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs into the next clue only for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Gore is spilt blood, and Al Gore served as American vice-president under Clinton.

clue.text: … acting so strangely, without any creative conviction

indicators.note: strangely says the letters are behaving oddly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Continuing from the last clue, a politician acting oddly and without belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creative' means creating, as in a Creator: the belief lacking is in a god.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic holds no firm belief in a deity, neither affirming nor denying one.

clue.text: Bay on American lake a secluded area once

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after the letters that follow it

parts.note: a cove is a small sheltered bay

explanation.surface: A bay beside an American lake, described as an old hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' looks like the definition, but it is the inlet COVE; the definition is the old sense at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcove once meant a garden bower or summerhouse, a secluded retreat; today it means a recess in a room.

clue.text: Embarrassed about my previous career

indicators.note: about means the colour word goes around the exclamation

parts.note: red, as in red-faced, means embarrassed
cor and my are both exclamations of surprise; cor is British slang

explanation.surface: Someone blushing about their past career.
explanation.definitionFit: A record is a person's history, such as a track record of past performance.

clue.text: Sportsperson first in park, exercising early

indicators.note: first in takes the opening letter of park
exercising means putting the letters through their paces, rearranging them

explanation.surface: An athlete who is first to the park for an early workout.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is someone who takes part in a sport or game.
